prompt: Write an email to a colleague about rumors going around town. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the email only.
final_message:
Subject: Heads up on what's going around

Hi Jordan,

I wanted to give you a quick heads up about some chatter I've been hearing around town lately, since I'd rather you hear it from me than get blindsided in a meeting.

The main rumor is that our largest local competitor is in talks to be acquired. People at the Chamber lunch last week were saying a regional firm has been circling for months, and that an announcement could come before the end of the year. I've also heard it might mean layoffs, but that part seems to be pure speculation. No one I spoke to could point to an actual source.

The second rumor is closer to home: that our own office might be moving downtown when the lease is up in the spring. A couple of people from the building's management company have apparently been touring spaces. I haven't seen anything official, and when I casually asked Dana in facilities, she said she hadn't heard a thing. That could mean it's nothing, or it could mean she's not in the loop yet.

Finally, there's talk that the city is going to approve the new development near the riverfront after all. If that happens, it would change traffic patterns and could affect a few of our client sites. Again, I'd treat this as unconfirmed until the council agenda comes out.

I want to be clear that I'm not treating any of this as fact. Rumors in a town this size tend to spread fast and get bigger with every retelling, and I'd hate for us to make decisions or say something to a client based on a story that turns out to be wrong. A couple of the details I've heard also contradict each other, which makes me even more skeptical.

That said, a few of these could matter for our planning, so I think it's worth keeping our ears open. If you hear anything concrete, especially about the competitor or the lease, would you let me know? I'll do the same. It might also be worth quietly asking leadership whether there's anything we should be prepared for, without making it sound like we're stirring the pot.

In the meantime, I'd suggest we keep this between us and not repeat any of it to the team or clients. No sense in creating worry over something that may never happen.

Let's catch up later this week. I'm free Thursday afternoon if you want to compare notes over coffee.

Thanks,
[name]
